svg.title: Spine platform architecture
svg.desc: Surfaces, deterministic comprehension and research over the Product Knowledge Graph, typed planning, a governed execution loop with two human gates, and SDLC delivery to a reviewed pull request. Generated from source at version 3.19.0.
svg.text: A request flows top to bottom — through comprehension, deterministic research and planning,
into an execution loop that pauses at two human gates — and out as a reviewed pull request.
You ask for something — from a terminal, your AI assistant, the web inbox, or the TUI. Same engine behind all four.
Claude Code & Codex call it as tools
the operator inbox — approvals live here
Before writing anything, Spine reads. Your requirement becomes structured intents; your code and your docs become a graph.
languages, framework, what kind of job
Every fact points at a file and a line. 8 node kinds · 11 edge kinds, across 8 language front-ends,
built from code and docs. No LLM — the same commit always gives the same graph. Everything above and
Every run starts here. Three deterministic passes compose one Evidence artifact, and everything after is judged against it.
blast radius keyed off the landing sites
criteria bound to a file:line, or refused
The work becomes a typed, validated plan — which tools, which budget, where the approvals sit. Not free-form prompting.
Stop. A human approves before a single line is generated — nothing has been written yet.
Now it runs. Each step is one contract-checked call, verified by 6 verifiers against schema, evidence and policy.
only at the moment of use
Code is generated grounded in what already exists and in the Evidence above, tested, and retried until the tests pass. Then it's reviewed.
Stop again. Until this moment nothing has been pushed to your repo or your tracker.
the pipeline ends here · deployment stays yours
Every step above was traced and recorded — an append-only trail you can replay, and a Case you can
read back node by node with `sdlc explain`.
Human gate — nothing crosses without you
